title: Commercial model and lifecycle agreements for enterprise private/VPC deployments
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Summary:
Define a repeatable commercial model and lifecycle agreement for enterprise Private/VPC and on-prem deployments. Objective is to create pricing constructs, support tiers, upgrade cadence options, and an enterprise negotiation playbook that scales across small enterprise pilots and 1000+ seat contracts.

Background:
Customers deploying Redwood Private ask for predictable TCO, clear upgrade windows, and SLAs that cover security-driven change control. Current ad-hoc deals lead to inconsistent pricing, long sales cycles, and churn risk at upgrades. We need a standardized offering that still allows seat-level negotiation for strategic accounts.

Proposed commercial constructs (experiment matrix):
- Base license fee: annual platform license covering control plane & core runtime binaries. Options: Flat-teired (Starter/Enterprise/Platform) OR usage-linked (base + per-GPU or per-concurrent-seat).
- Capacity add-ons: reserved GPU pools (monthly commit) with burst credits. Pricing anchored to $/GPU-hour equivalent in hosted market.
- Support tiers: Essential (business hours email, 48h patches), Enhanced (24/7 support, 8h critical SLA, quarterly health review), Concierge (dedicated TAM, 2h critical SLA, on-site quarterly).
- Upgrade cadence and policy: Standard customers receive quarterly minor patches and 12-month major releases; Extended maintenance (paid add-on) supports 24-month upgrade deferral plus limited security backports; Emergency hotfix SLA for security incidents included in Enhanced+.
- Professional services and onboarding: fixed scoping packages (30/60/90 day) priced separately.

Decision criteria for proposals:
- Time-to-close improvement target: 25% faster for pilot deals.
- Renewal retention target: reduce upgrade-related churn by 50% across pilot cohort.
- Legal/InfoSec acceptance target: 80% of RFPs satisfied without custom contract amendments.

Experiment plan:
1) Pilot cohort (3 customers): offer two commercial tracks (Tiered-flat vs Base+capacity). Monitor sales velocity, negotiation points, and legal redlines.
2) Support tier A/B test: two pilots on Enhanced vs Concierge to measure incident resolution satisfaction and cost delta.
3) Offer limited-time extended maintenance add-on to 4 customers to gauge demand for delayed upgrades.

Metrics to track:
- Sales cycle length (days)
- Contracts requiring SOW or custom SLAs (count)
- Negotiated discount vs list price (median)
- Upgrade deferral requests and churn at upgrade windows
- Time-to-respond for security questionnaire items (days)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Too many commercial permutations increases legal overhead. Mitigation: Limit permutations to 3 baseline bundles + 2 add-ons.
- Risk: Extended maintenance increases security surface and operational burden. Mitigation: Require contractually-defined security backport window and charge premium for extended maintenance.
- Risk: Market pushback on per-GPU pricing vs per-seat. Mitigation: Provide calculators and benchmarks comparing hosted unit economics.

Deliverables:
- Pricing matrix and example SOW templates (for three typical deployment sizes).
- Standard contract amendment language for upgrade windows and backports.
- Security questionnaire response library (90% coverage for common enterprise questionnaires).
- Pilot negotiation playbook and one-pager for Sales/SEs.

Next steps:
- Align with Legal and Security on standard amendment wording (week 1).
- Run pilot offers with 3 committed customers in March-April (week 2-6).
- Collect negotiation and RFP feedback, iterate on pricing and support tiers (week 7-10).
